title: KV cache approximation layers: FP8/INT8/INT4 fidelity experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Evaluate a layered approximation strategy for KV cache storage to reduce GPU RAM while bounding generation quality regressions. Instead of a single global quant format, we will experiment with an "approximation ladder" that stores hot token cohorts in higher-precision (FP16 or FP8) and colder cohorts in INT8/INT4 with compact packing.

Background: Prior work at Redwood explored single-format KV quantization (FP8-only, INT8-only). Those experiments showed non-linear quality degradation for long-context, multi-turn chat where certain tokens in KV are high-leverage for next-token logits. We want a practical middle ground: store most entries in extremely compact form but preserve fidelity for cache entries identified as high-impact by a lightweight attention-saliency heuristic.

Goals:
- Measure end-to-end generation quality impact (perplexity, downstream task F1, and human eval on tricky prompts) across FP8/INT8/INT4 mixes.
- Quantify GPU memory reduction and throughput improvements under continuous-batching regimes typical of production traffic.
- Validate a cohort-aware fallback policy that dynamically promotes degraded entries during rollout to reduce p99 latency regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identify at least one hybrid configuration that reduces KV RAM by >=40% vs baseline FP16 with <=2% drop in automated quality metrics on our evaluation suite and no significant increase in p99 latency for 95% of customer traces.
- Produce a rollout playbook (safety gates, metrics, fallback logic) and an implementation PR that can be A/B tested behind the Dedicated autoscaler.
decisions: Use a three-tier approximation ladder: tier0=FP16/FP8 (hot), tier1=INT8 (warm), tier2=INT4 (cold, block-packed).
Identify hot entries using a rolling attention-energy heuristic sampled per-request to keep compute overhead <3%.
Do not modify model weights; this is storage-only transformation applied at runtime cache insertion/eviction.
Implement decode-time lightweight dequantization with eager path for tier0 and on-demand promotion for tier1/2 to avoid p99 amplification.
experiment_plan: Dataset: mix of Redwood internal long-context chat traces (100k conversations), WebQA benchmark slices, and curated adversarial prompts (3k).
Metrics: token-level cross-entropy, seq-level next-token accuracy, generation BLEU/ROUGE for structured tasks, and a 1-5 human rating on 800 sampled generations.
Configs to test: baseline FP16, FP8-only, INT8-only, INT4-blockpacked-only, hybrid ladder (FP8/INT8/INT4) with 3 heuristics for hot-detection (attention-energy, recency, reply-sensitivity).
Memory/Perf: measure peak GPU KV memory, per-token throughput under continuous batching with batch window 25ms, and p50/p95/p99 latency for 128B and 1kB sequences.
Fidelity stress tests: long multi-turn (>8 turns) and long-generation (>1024 tokens) scenarios to surface cascading degradation.
Safety checks: ensure numerical stability for softmax logits; run divergence checks vs FP16 on first 500 tokens of selected traces.
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Prototype quant/dequant routines implemented in runtime bench harness (bench-v2). Basic INT8 and block-packed INT4 encode/decode validated against FP16 on synthetic tensors (relative error profiles logged).
2025-11-07: Attention-energy heuristic implemented as a sampling shim; overhead measured ~1.8% CPU and 2.1% GPU time on microbenchmarks. Added metric capture for per-entry hazard score.

2025-11-10: Ran first hybrid ladder sweep on 10k chat traces. Observed 38% KV RAM reduction for hybrid config A with average perplexity delta +1.9%. p99 latency increased by 6% in cold-path heavy traces.

2025-11-13: PM review (Clara Jensen) requested human eval on edge cases (hallucination patterns). Added targeted adversarial set. Added dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-approx/kv-approx-summary (internal).

2025-11-16: Implementation PR opened for in-runtime tiering and promotion logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147 (WIP). Added confluence runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/987654321/KV+Approximation+Ladder+Runbook
comments: PM Clara Jensen: Good start — need clearer rollback criteria for customer traffic and gating thresholds for dedicated vs hosted tiers.
Design review (Kai Nguyen): Consider exposing a per-customer fidelity knob in Console that maps to ladder aggressiveness; UX notes linked in runbook.
Eng review (Sofia Martinez): Edge-case: INT4 block unpacking increases memory pressure transiently during promotion. Suggest using streaming promotion (page in 256-entry slices).
Security (Ravi Shah): Confirmed no secret material in KV stores; encryption pipeline unaffected but we should validate KMS throughput under extra dequant ops.
risks: Quality cliff: small cohorts of high-leverage tokens might be quantized aggressively causing sharp downstream accuracy/regression on few customers.
Latency variance: on-demand promotion could spike p99 if promotion falls during critical request windows.
Operational complexity: additional telemetry and fallback policies increase alert surface and require updated runbooks.
next_steps: Complete full-suite sweep (100k traces) for the three heuristics and select top-2 configs by cost-quality tradeoff (target by 2025-11-22).
Add streaming promotion prototype to avoid large transient allocations; benchmark p99 impact.
Coordinate with Console team to add a fidelity toggle and with Customer Success for early pilot customers.
Merge PR once internal benchmarks meet gate and begin A/B rollout on Dedicated cluster with conservative traffic slices.
